simple.meaning: אָצַל (ʼâtsal) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, to join ; used only as a denominative from 681 ; to separate ; hence, to select , refuse , contract.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אָצַל (H680) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 27:36, with occurrences in Genesis, Numbers, Ecclesiastes, Ezekiel.

definitions.short: properly, to join ; used only as a denominative from 681 ; to separate ; hence, to select , refuse , contract
definitions.full: H680. atsal [ אָצַל ] verb denominative lay aside, reserve, withdraw, withhold — Qal Perfect אָצַלְתָּ Gen 27:36 ; אָצַלְתִּי Eccl 2:10 ; וְאָֽצַלְתִּ֫י consecutive Num 11:17 ; — reserve , בְרָכָה לִי Gen 27:36 ; ( withdraw ), set apart מִןהָֿרוּחַ Num 11:17 ; withhold מֵהֶם Eccl 2:10 . Niph`al Perfect נֶאֱצַל Ezek 42:6 be withdrawn , i.e. shortened or narrowed. Hiph`il Imperfect וַיָּאצֶל Num 11:25 (Kö 1. 390 ) = Qal 11:17 .

occurrences.englishText: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”

I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you don’t bear it yourself alone.
Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more.
Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
For they were in three stories, and they didn’t have pillars as the pillars of the courts. Therefore the uppermost was set back more than the lowest and the middle from the ground.
